A web article can reach the reader without a single image. The page is fetched as static HTML, its main content is extracted, and the result becomes the same semantic document a Markdown file produces. This paragraph gives the readability algorithm enough prose to pick the article body, and it names no heading of its own.

Typography, themes and reading position come from the reader rather than from the page, so a plain article still sets publication-quality text. The second paragraph exists to keep the candidate score above the extractor's threshold and to give the export more than one block to lay out.
